context:
2026-11-11 investigation (read-only). It recurs, so the 'close as not recurring' gate does not apply and this item is no longer part of feature-test-fixture-and-ci-shard-hygiene-20261111. `medium-test (shard 2)` was cancelled at about 25.3 minutes (the job's timeout-minutes) in at least 16 other runs between 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-10, including 42431461560, 42516417430, 42529875736, 42536578036, 42536595566, 42639754221, 42737669789, 42742663123, 42748075993, 42830090786, 42832274025, 42836892175, 42844094574, 42845777079; two were the trunk-lane-plain variant. Only shard 2 is affected. The scan went back to 2026-11-05 and hit its time limit, so there may be more. In run 43041683685 the shard progressed to about 98 percent and then the workers sat idle until the timeout; the other runs' logs were not opened. A normal shard takes 8 minutes or less, so raising the timeout would only delay the cancellation: the likely cause is a test or teardown that hangs in shard 2's slice. Next step: compare shard 2's assigned test ids across two of these runs, find the test that never finishes, and reproduce that slice locally with verbose output (heavy work: use the lock-taking entry point). Each failure costs a 25-minute wait plus a rerun.

2026-11-11 18:23Z: it happened again on PR #4112 head ccb161b11, run 43070371531: `medium-test (shard 2)` cancelled at the timeout with two pytest-xdist workers alive for over 20 minutes at low load (load average 0.11), then `core` failed at 'Verify complete medium shard coverage' because shard-2-execution.json was missing. `make pr-status PR=4112` shows the worker process table from the job log. Re-run once with `make pr-rerun PR=4112`.

2026-11-11 root cause (read-only analysis of nine failing and three passing shard-2 job logs, saved as /tmp/shard2-<job>.log on the investigating machine). Two parts. (1) Trigger: `kill_with_watchdog` in tests/unit/utils/test_heavy_watchdog.py runs `Watchdog._kill_tree` inside the pytest worker with a policy whose holder is `os.getpid()` and whose budget is 1 GiB. After killing the wrapper subtree, `_kill_tree` re-samples the holder's tree, which always includes the root process, and if the worker itself is over 1 GiB `_terminate_holder` sends it SIGTERM then SIGKILL. Every failing log has exactly one 'node down: Not properly terminated' about three minutes in, the dying worker is always the larger one (1.62-1.91 GiB RSS), the crash position matches this file's scope in all seven distinct node lists checked, and no passing log has a worker death. Reproduced outside pytest: the same call exits 0 at 0.2 GiB and is killed by SIGTERM (exit 143) at 1.3 GiB. The helper arrived in 525361b2 (#3972, 2026-11-06); failures start 2026-11-08. (2) Hang: pytest-xdist 3.8.0 with `--dist loadscope` cannot finish a session after a worker dies (upstream pytest-dev/pytest-xdist#1378, fixed on master, not yet released): finished scopes are re-queued as empty batches that never complete, so both workers idle until the job timeout. Only shard 2 because the sharder assigns whole files and this file always lands there. Unproven: which of the four tests using the helper fires it, and the worker's exact unique memory at the crash. Fix plan: build the helper's policy with a zero budget so the holder is never terminated (none of the four tests checks the budget), and pass `--max-worker-restart=0` to the medium pytest command so any future worker crash ends the session in seconds and names the test.

2026-11-11: fix committed as c42461212e on branch fix/watchdog-test-kills-xdist-worker (worktree /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox.wt-fix-watchdog-test-kills-worker): zero budget in kill_with_watchdog, and --max-worker-restart=0 in the medium pytest command of ci.yml, trunk.yml and trunk-coverage.yml. Problem. On PR #4100 head 87096f7e, `medium-test (shard 2)` of CI run 43041683685 ran from 14:49:02Z to 15:14:19Z and ended `cancelled`; the other three shards succeeded and `core` then failed because of it. Nothing cancelled it by hand. `make pr-rerun` re-ran the run and the shard passed. One observation, so the cause is unknown: a job timeout, a runner loss, or concurrency cancellation.

Change. Establish the cause from the job log and the workflow's timeout and concurrency settings. If it is a timeout near the shard's normal duration, raise the margin or rebalance; if it is concurrency, fix the group.
